notes: THREE REQUESTS. 1. SALARY AND CARD NO LONGER PRINT Rs 0 FOR FUTURE MONTHS. Those cells asserted that the salary account will be empty and the card settled — assumptions the model makes, not balances — inside a section labelled as live. A live balance is a present-tense fact, so a future column has nothing to report and now shows a dash. Savings keeps a projected figure there, because the chain genuinely computes one. No calculation changed; the close, the chain and every downstream page are untouched. 2. INSTRUMENTS CAN NOW BE CLOSED FROM EDIT INPUTS. Investigation first: EMI rows on that page ALREADY carried a timeline control for step-up and close-early, and the timeline editor already supported investments — it had simply never been wired onto the investment rows. So the gap was one missing button rather than a page's worth of functionality. Investment rows now carry the same control, with the badge marking instruments that already have lifecycle events, and readInvestments already preserved those events so the save path needed no change. Verified: the control appears on every row, the badge marks a closed FD, the modal opens offering close-and-redeem, and events survive a save round trip. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: the Instruments page was NOT deleted. The request was to remove it, but nothing is gained by deleting a page over simply not visiting it, and deleting it risks losing capability neither of us has audited. Partial and full redemptions are transactions and already belong in the Journal. If the page proves genuinely redundant after some use, it can be removed then with evidence rather than on assumption. 3. INPUT FIELDS GIVEN MORE ROOM, globally rather than per page: padding 12/14 to 14/16, minimum height 48px, body font 14 to 16px and monospace numeric fields 13 to 15px with slight letter spacing. The 16px base also stops iOS zooming the viewport when a field takes focus. Regression confirms the Projection-to-Dashboard and Decisions-to-chain gaps both remain zero. No page errors.
